mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 anticipates higher future discount rates, which compresses the present value of expected corporate earnings and drives negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where FEDFUNDS rises >0.25pp, SPX 20d returns are non-negative with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test against the null of no effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE for three consecutive months is interpreted as labor market softening, which reduces the real wage growth expected by firms and leads to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 60-day windows where UNRATE falls for 3 months, SPX 60d returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST index exceeds 1,300 units for two consecutive months, it indicates elevated consumer demand, which raises expected future corporate profits and produces positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 5-day windows triggered by the HOUST threshold, SPX 5d returns are negative with p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in INDPRO above 104 (index 2017=100) for one month signals supply-side expansion, which typically precedes a temporary S&P 500 20-day bull run as market participants anticipate excess capacity.
failure_condition: During 20-day windows following INDPRO > 104, SPX 20d returns are flat with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises by more than 10,000 persons in a month, it reflects strong labor market absorption, which boosts corporate hiring plans and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: In 60-day windows with PAYEMS > +10,000, SPX 60d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising GDPC1 above 24,000 suggest robust demand for consumer goods, which elevates expected future earnings and yields positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: During 20-day windows with GDPC1 > 24,000 for 2 months, SPX 20d returns are negative with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE for a month creates a dual headwind that suppresses growth expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE decline, SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-inflation-cool period (CPIAUCSL < 324), S&P 500 5-day forward returns tend to be positive as markets price in easing cost pressures and potential rate cuts.
failure_condition: In 5-day windows with CPIAUCSL < 324, SPX 5d returns are non-positive with p-value > 0.05.
